text:
Support-Liaison: Heads-up — multiple EU customers reporting a p95 jump (~100-300ms increase) starting ~2026-03-16 15:12 UTC for /v1/generate (eu-west). Reports mention TLS handshake spikes and occasional 504s. Opening thread and tagging oncall @SRE-Oncall @Noah

SRE-Oncall: On it. Do we have any quick repro (curl/traceroute) from customers? Are backend queues or CPU showing anything?

Support-Liaison: Customers pasted a quick curl run:
```
$ curl -v -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer} %{http_code}\n" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -o /dev/null
* TLS handshake took 0.280s
* time_connect 0.045 time_starttransfer 0.325 200
```
They say this used to be ~0.06s for handshake.

Noah: Running internal probes now. Quick traceroute from probe-eu1 (15:18 UTC):
```
1  edge-eu1 10 ms
2  edge-proxy-az3 12 ms
3  transit-ixX 230 ms 
4  gslb-192.redwood.net 240 ms
5  origin-eu-west 245 ms
```
Looks like some traffic is being steered via an unexpected transit (hop 3).

Olivia: Observability confirm — p95 for eu-west increased from ~80ms to ~320ms at 15:10 UTC. TLS handshake histogram shows a mode shift 30ms -> 250ms. No CPU saturation on inference hosts.

SRE-Oncall: Any control-plane or routing changes around 15:00? @Netops-Bot can you dump rollout events? :rotating_light:

Netops-Bot: geo-steering rollout event detected: id=gs-1023 applied at 2026-03-16T15:05:12Z. Targets: EU -> dynamic steering policy. Rollout percentage increased 05%->30% between 15:05-15:12. Health-check sensitivity change also applied.

Noah: That matches timing. My AS-path checks show some sessions being steered to a transit that exits via an AS in SA region for a subset of prefixes — likely due to the new health sensitivity misclassifying eu-west edges as unhealthy for some prefixes.

Olivia: We see corresponding increase in cross-AZ egress and an extra ~200ms RTT on those paths. TLS handshake inflation correlates with the longer RTT and additional network hop.

SRE-Oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) rollback geo-steering policy to previous stable config for EU, 2) pin traffic for affected customers to primary eu-west pop for 30m, 3) increase client timeouts for affected support tickets, 4) follow-up RCA on health-check thresholds. Rolling rollback now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Netops-Bot: Rollback initiated (gs-1023 -> gs-1023-rollback) at 2026-03-16T15:30:05Z. Progress: 0%->100% within 7m.

Netops-Bot: Rollback complete at 2026-03-16T15:37:23Z.

Olivia: Post-rollback metrics: p95 back to ~95ms within 8 minutes. TLS handshake histogram shifting back to pre-incident baseline. Monitoring alarms cleared for eu-west handshake spike.

Support-Liaison: Customer A confirmed restored. Customer B still sees rare spikes — asked them for traceroute and raw curl output.

SRE-Oncall: Good. Action items: 1) Noah to correlate AS-paths with provider for the abnormal transit and ask provider to investigate, 2) Olivia to run expanded synthetic probes across all EU edge pairs for 24h and add guardrail alerts on geo-steering rollouts, 3) add a safe-limit to rollout automation to prevent cross-continent steering >10% without manual review. Assigning Noah/Olivia.

Noah: Acknowledged. I'll pull AS-paths and open ticket with transit vendor + share BGP dump. :thumbsup:

Olivia: I'll keep probes running and draft short post-incident note. If Customer B still repros after I collect their traces we'll open a follow-up.

SRE-Oncall: Thanks all. Leaving thread here for follow-up items. If anything new appears, ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
